catalog.description: Semantic catalog of every regular file under images/ in the Sonic Physics Guide repository: annotated documentation diagrams and captures, level-map illustrations, two character spritesheets, inline glyphs, wiki page furniture and two emulator overlay scripts.
method_notes: Produced in two passes. Pass 1: recursive inventory, SHA-256, container-level media facts parsed from file headers by scripts/catalog.py (format decided by content signature, not extension), Markdown backlinks and duplicate detection. Pass 2: visual inspection of every file and semantic description.

Visual inspection was performed by an AI model viewing the images. Still images were viewed in full. Animated files with 8 frames or fewer were viewed frame by frame; longer ones were sampled at 12, 16 or 20 evenly spaced frames (the exact frame numbers are recorded in verification.inspected_frames). Events between sampled frames were not observed, and sequence transitions may only cite inspected frames.

Field ownership: sha256, media, related_docs, provenance.source_pages and the exact-duplicate relationships are DERIVED by `python3 scripts/catalog.py sync` and re-verified by `validate`. All other fields are authored and never rewritten by the tool.

The summary and depicts fields record only what is visible. Statements from repository documentation are recorded under demonstrates with basis "documentation"; readings that neither the file nor the text confirms carry basis "inferred". Numbers read off images are transcribed by eye and flagged numeric-values-unverified.

GIF transparency: many GIFs declare a transparent palette index, typically for delta frames. Composited opacity of all 50 GIFs was checked once with an independent image decoder during cataloguing; no composited frame contained transparent pixels. The tool records only the header-level declaration (alpha.mode) and leaves pixel-level fields null for those files.

Atlas frame regions are recorded only where they are reproducible: for sprites.sonic1-sheet-transparent they are tight bounds of 8-connected opaque pixel groups, and `validate` re-measures them from the file. Pose names, animation order, durations, mirroring rules and pivots are not in any file and are marked as requiring manual review.

rights_status is a cataloguing label, not legal advice. restricted-or-unclear means the file depicts or is composed of commercial game imagery and no license, author or permission is recorded in the repository. unknown means nothing at all is recorded.

Seven files have a content type that differs from their extension (six GIFs named .png/.PNG and one JPEG named .png). They are catalogued by their actual content and flagged; no file was renamed or re-encoded.
open_questions: Sonic1_Spritesheet.png and Sonic1_Spritesheet_Transparent.png were added by hand and described as a "raw rip" with no source, ripper or permission recorded. Rights are unknown and are the largest redistribution risk in the repository.

docs/23-implementation-guide.md and README.md describe the spritesheet contents row by row (including Peel-Out frames) in a way that does not match the observed 16-column x 6-row layout and that contradicts docs/16-special-abilities.md, which attributes Peel-Out to Sonic CD. Pose names, order, timing, mirroring and pivots need manual establishment before any runtime use.

About 100 wiki-scraped diagrams and captures are composed of commercial Sega game imagery; per-file source URLs, authors and license terms were never recorded and the Sonic Retro file pages were not fetched. Their redistribution status is unresolved.

The two Lua overlay scripts name their authors (@LapperDev, @MercurySilver) and cite download URLs in docs/22-overlay-scripts.md, but contain no license text, and how they entered images/ is not recorded.

Document-Icon.svg carries an "Uploaded to: SVG Repo" comment and Download.svg was made with Inkscape with no license element; neither is referenced by Markdown directly (only their 14 px and 35 px rasters are), and their licenses are unknown.
Seven files have the wrong extension for their content (see method notes); upstream naming or the scraper may need to be reviewed, but the originals were deliberately left untouched.
Four space-named files are byte-identical copies of underscore-named files; documentation alt text still uses the space-named form. Removing or referencing them is a repository decision left open.
